info.title: MAIC engine protocol
info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line, between MAIC's engine and every interface (docs/design/engine-protocol.md). Names are OpenAI's where OpenAI's API description defines the concept (protocol/openai/), MAIC's own under maic. and in a maic object. Every method here is in the engine's dispatcher and the reverse (ctest protocol_schema). x-maic-remote says whether a remote client may call it; x-maic-params on a notification is the schema of its whole params object; errors carry OpenAI's error object in data (schemas/maic.schema.json#/$defs/ErrorData).

methods.name: maic.hello
methods.summary: Opens the connection: the protocol version, who the client is, what it supports. Nothing else is accepted before it.

params.name: protocol
params.description: The highest protocol version the client speaks.

params.name: exclude
params.description: Event types the client does not want, from ordering.json's filter.filterable (the deltas: their item's done event carries what they did). A type the engine does not know is ignored; any other is refused with maic_not_filterable.

params.name: auth
params.description: Remote transports only: the token or the account's access token.

methods.name: maic.engine.status
methods.summary: What maic-server's GET /api/status answered: the harness, the model, the sessions loaded.

methods.name: maic.engine.trip
methods.summary: Trips the harness and cancels every response. Open to every client: stopping only adds restriction.

methods.name: maic.index.get
methods.summary: The session index: the loaded and parked sessions.

methods.name: maic.index.subscribe
methods.summary: maic.index notifications from now on.

methods.name: maic.index.unsubscribe
methods.summary: No more maic.index notifications.

methods.name: maic.session.list
methods.summary: Transcripts as `maic sessions` lists them, stopped ones included.

params.name: all
params.description: Every workspace, not only the engine's.

methods.name: createConversation
methods.summary: A new session (OpenAI's operationId). Remote: inside server.workspaces.

methods.name: getConversation
methods.summary: A session as OpenAI's conversation object, its index entry in maic.entry.

methods.name: maic.session.resume
methods.summary: Loads a transcript as a live session again: by id or a unique prefix (a path only locally).

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

params.name: leave
params.description: What happens to the session the client's focus leaves: `bg`, `park`, `stop`, or `default` (the session's `leave.switch` setting for an idle or a working one, unless another client has it in focus; `maic_leave_ask` when that case is `ask`). A session left working gets the case's `after` (park or stop once its work ends with no client in focus). Without `leave` it goes to the background.

methods.name: maic.session.fork
methods.summary: A second session from this one's transcript (its first `at` records, default all of it), by pointer; it starts as any session does, and its epoch names its parent's.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

params.name: leave
params.description: What happens to the session the client's focus leaves: `bg`, `park`, `stop`, or `default` (the session's `leave.switch` setting for an idle or a working one, unless another client has it in focus; `maic_leave_ask` when that case is `ask`). A session left working gets the case's `after` (park or stop once its work ends with no client in focus). Without `leave` it goes to the background.

methods.name: maic.session.focus
methods.summary: `:switch`: the client's focus moves to a loaded session (maic.session.resume loads a parked one).

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

params.name: leave
params.description: What happens to the session the client's focus leaves: `bg`, `park`, `stop`, or `default` (the session's `leave.switch` setting for an idle or a working one, unless another client has it in focus; `maic_leave_ask` when that case is `ask`). A session left working gets the case's `after` (park or stop once its work ends with no client in focus). Without `leave` it goes to the background.

methods.name: maic.session.background
methods.summary: `:bg`: the client lets go of the session; it keeps working, live while another client has it in focus.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: maic.session.leave
methods.summary: `:q`: what the client's going does to the session in its focus, now, before it closes: `as`, else the session's `leave.quit` for an idle or a working one, unless another client has it in focus. Where sessions do not outlive their clients (no daemon), one that would stay loaded does what `leave.no_daemon` says, and so does every session in the background. A connection that ends without it leaves as `default`.

params.name: as
params.description: `bg`, `park`, `stop`, or `default` (the session's `leave.quit`). A session left working in the background gets `leave.quit.after`.

left.description: The entry of the session left, as it is now; null when the client had none in focus.

methods.name: maic.session.park
methods.summary: Ends the session for now: it leaves memory, stays in the index with the messages that waited to run, and resumes where it was. maic_busy while a response runs, unless `interrupt`.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: maic.session.stop
methods.summary: Ends the session: it leaves the index and stays an ordinary transcript (a parked one can be stopped too). maic_busy while a response runs, unless `interrupt`.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: maic.session.attach
methods.summary: A snapshot of the session, and its events from the snapshot's sequence_number on, in one step.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: listConversationItems
methods.summary: OpenAI's: a page of the conversation's history from its transcript, after an item, newest first unless order is asc; maic.exchanges pages by exchanges instead of limit.

params.name: conversation_id
params.description: A session id.

params.name: after
params.description: An item id; the page starts past it in the order asked.

params.name: include
params.description: Accepted as OpenAI's; history has nothing more to include.

methods.name: getConversationItem
methods.summary: OpenAI's: one item of the conversation's history, collapsed over the client's collapse_over as a page is.

params.name: conversation_id
params.description: A session id.

params.name: include
params.description: Accepted as OpenAI's.

methods.name: maic.item.expand
methods.summary: Up to 256 KiB of a history item's text from offset: a tool's recorded result, an attached file, a message.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id.

params.name: offset
params.description: In bytes; a part starts on a character.

methods.name: maic.session.subscribe
methods.summary: The session's events after starting_after, replayed from the ring, then as they come. maic_resync when they left the ring or the epoch changed.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

params.name: epoch
params.description: The epoch the client's numbers belong to (attach's and subscribe's answers name it); another epoch answers maic_resync.

params.name: starting_after
params.description: The last sequence_number the client holds; -1 or absent for the whole ring.

methods.name: maic.session.unsubscribe
methods.summary: No more of the session's events.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: maic.session.set
methods.summary: Changes one session's settings for every client, announced in maic.session.settings with `by`.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

params.name: mode
params.description: A remote client tightens freely and loosens up to edit; auto needs a step-up.

params.name: confirm
params.description: Auto under a dumb harness answers maic_confirm_required until a local client confirms it.

methods.x-maic-remote-partly: mode: tighten freely, loosen up to edit; auto only after a step-up (refused until accounts register a verifier)

methods.name: response.create
methods.summary: Input on a session's lane: starts a turn when the session is idle and resumes a paused one. On a busy lane the response waits behind the running one (FIFO, status queued); a message for the running response is response.steer. With maic.now the input goes into the running response at once.

params.name: stream_id
params.description: The lane: the session id.

params.name: conversation
params.description: The session, as OpenAI names a conversation.

params.name: input
params.description: Required unless maic.now asks to deliver what is already queued.

params.name: instructions
params.description: Local clients only.

params.name: maic
params.description: MAIC's own: `now` delivers the input into the running response at once, its model call abandoned (`:w now`); with no input, what is already queued goes in now.

methods.name: cancelResponse
methods.summary: Ends the running response (or a paused turn, by its last response), its partial output kept; the turn ends with it. A response still waiting on the lane is taken off it. Open to every client.

methods.name: response.steer
methods.summary: OpenAI's steering: queues user input for the running response (or a paused turn's last, which it resumes). response.steer.accepted follows; the response finishes at its next boundary with response.incomplete (steered) and a successor's response.created commits the input.

params.name: previous_response_id
params.description: The running response, or a paused turn's last.

methods.name: maic.steer
methods.summary: One of the six steering actions on a running response (section 11): steer, drop and further redirect with a note, interrupt pauses the turn, keep accepts the partial reply, halt discards it. The action must be in steering.actions and allowed for the client's side (maic_steer_disabled).

params.name: response_id
params.description: The running response, or a paused turn's last.

params.name: note
params.description: Text for the model: steer's direction, drop's and further's addition. A note is input: a remote one raises the turn's origin.

params.name: trim
params.description: drop: how much of the partial reply goes; steering.drop_trim by default.

params.name: at
params.description: drop: the byte offset in the partial reply to cut from, chosen in the client; overrides trim.

params.name: tool
params.description: steer and drop: a running tool is cancelled, or waited for; steering.on_running_tool by default.

params.name: step_up
params.description: The step-up proof the airtight tier asks of a remote client (step 18).

methods.name: maic.approval.answer
methods.summary: Answers an approval. The first valid answer wins; a late one is maic_already_answered. A remote client cannot answer always.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

params.name: feedback
params.description: For no: a sentence for the model.

methods.name: maic.question.reply
methods.summary: Answers the model's question.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: updateConversation
methods.summary: Renames a session (`:rename`): its title, announced in maic.session.title.

methods.name: maic.session.command
methods.summary: A `:` command the engine owns, typed into any client (`line`, without its colon), or the answer to a question one asked (`ask` and `key`). Its events come as it causes them.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

params.name: line
params.description: The command line without its colon: "ban add foo".

params.name: ask
params.description: The id of a question a command asked.

params.name: key
params.description: The answer: one of the question's keys.

methods.x-maic-remote-partly: :mode (tightening freely, loosening up to edit), :model, :think, :compact, :rename, :todo, :tools, :status, adding a :forbid term, lowering :budget and :trip; every other command, and a command's question, are local only

methods.name: maic.session.shell
methods.summary: `!cmd`: runs `command` in the user's own shell, unsandboxed, in the session's workspace; its output streams as maic.tool.output.delta with no output_index, and what it printed reaches the model as context. Answered when it ends. `interrupt` stops the one running.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: maic.approval.proposed
methods.summary: A waiting write's content after it, for a diff beside the approval (maic.approval.requested carries only proposed_size).

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: maic.session.describe
methods.summary: What a session loaded: its instruction files, its tools and the notices about them, for an interface's welcome.

params.name: session
params.description: A session id (a side thread's or a task's id works too).

methods.name: maic.event
methods.summary: One session event, exactly as the Responses WebSocket would send it, with sequence_number and stream_id. Its params are the event: x-maic-params is its schema, the union over type.

methods.name: maic.index
methods.summary: An index entry changed or left; replaces state, carries no sequence_number.

methods.name: maic.engine
methods.summary: Engine-wide: the tripwire, or a protocol fault the guarded tier logged.
